rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery`. I found no gap, though one boundary (below) is thinly covered.

- **Defaults of `new`:**
  - It asserts `query.limit == None` and `query.context_lines == 0` directly on a fresh `TextQuery::new`.
  - The default scope is exercised by searching without a scope. That search returns all 3 matches, across both `one.txt` and `two.txt`.
  - The default context is also checked by the excerpts. Each excerpt starts with `hit` and has length 4, so only the matching line is returned.
- **`pattern` is a regex:** The pattern `^hit[0-9]$` uses anchors and a character class. It matches `hit1`, `hit2` and `hit3` but not `middle`.
- **`limit(n)` override and bounding:**
  - `limit(2)` over the default scope, which spans two files, yields exactly 2 matches and `complete == false`. That shows the limit applies across the scope rather than per file.
  - A scoped query with limit 2 and exactly 2 matches stays `complete`.
  - `scoped.limit(1)` yields 1 match and an incomplete result.
  - The unlimited default returns all matches.
- **`scope(...)` override:** After `.scope(SourceScope::under("one.txt"))`, the entries contain only `one.txt` paths. The `two.txt` match is excluded.
- **`context_lines(1)` override:** The exact entries are `(one.txt, 1, "hit1\nmiddle")` and `(one.txt, 3, "middle\nhit2")`. The first match shows only trailing context, since it is at the start of the file. The second shows only leading context, since it is at the end. Together they exercise the context window in both directions, with line numbers.
- **Public API:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported surface, including the type and its builder methods, against rustdoc.

The context test only uses the value 1, and no single match has context on both sides. I did not count this as a gap. Positive values are one input class, and the two directional cases would catch an off-by-one in either direction.

The other tests that use `TextQuery` (in `sources/tests.rs` and `agent/tests.rs`) are not marked as tests of this requirement, so I did not rely on them.

text: `TextQuery::new(pattern)` searches all visible files, with zero context lines and
no match limit. `scope`, `context_lines`, and `limit` override those defaults.

`pattern` is a regular expression. `context_lines` requests that many lines on either side of each matching line. Zero returns just the matching line. `limit` bounds matches across the scope. `None` requests all matches.
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn context_lines(self, context_lines: usize) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
